findings.title: NPE when all-clients resource is missing in per-client check
findings.body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) when no per-client resource is found it falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource for Clients. That helper can return null, for example on upgraded realms without a Clients resource or if it was deleted. The code then calls findByResource(server, resource) with null without a null check, causing NullPointerException and HTTP 500 on admin client endpoints instead of safely denying access.

findings.title: Global client grant ignored when per-client resource exists
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) evaluates only one resource: if a per-client resource exists it evaluates only that resource, otherwise it evaluates the all-clients resource. If a per-client resource was created for one scope like view, a check for another scope like manage or map-roles on the same client will evaluate only the per-client policies and ignore a valid all-clients grant, incorrectly denying access. Correct authorization requires OR of per-object and all-type grants.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission never finds per-client resources
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with only name and owner and never sets the Resource type, so their type is null. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission enumerates candidates with findByType for Clients type, which only matches the single all-clients resource. Per-client grants are therefore never enumerated, and the global resource name Clients which is not a client id would be added to the result, so filtered client listing with per-client permissions returns empty or wrong results.

findings.title: Global canView ignores MANAGE grant
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.canView without arguments returns true only for view permission, while canView for client scopes checks view or manage and per-client canView is true via canConfigure and canManage. An admin granted only manage on all clients will have canManage true but canView false, so global list and view checks deny managers who should be able to view. This is inconsistent with the transitive manage-implies-view behavior expected for users and scopes.

findings.title: NPE on invalid resourceType in getScope
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType exists. If resourceType is null or unknown the get returns null and getScopes throws NullPointerException resulting in HTTP 500. It should throw ModelValidationException with 400 like other schema validations for bad permission input.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle Clients type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName special-cases only Users to return All users or username. For Clients it falls through to resource.getDisplayName, but per-client resources created by getOrCreateResource have no display name set and are named by internal UUID. Admin UI and permission display for client permissions will therefore show null or UUID instead of All clients or clientId.

findings.title: init does not migrate existing realms for new Clients type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early if the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms created before this change never get the new Clients scopes and all-clients resource. Creating a client permission on such realms then fails scope lookup with ModelException No scopes found, and global client checks return false. Upgrade needs to add missing scopes and type resources to existing clients.

findings.title: Permission cleanup disabled and broken for V2
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener now only runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ V1 is enabled. With only V2 enabled, deletion of clients, roles and groups leaks V2 authorization resources and policies because setPermissionsEnabled is never called. With both V1 and V2 enabled, management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client, role or group will fail with 500.

findings.title: V2 evaluator throws 500 for unsupported operations
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2 implements methods like canExchangeTo, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions by throwing raw UnsupportedOperationException. When admin REST management endpoints or token-exchange checks call these in V2 mode the exception becomes HTTP 500 instead of a proper deny or 400 error, breaking API contract and availability.

findings.title: Wrong Javadoc for void require methods
findings.body: ClientPermissionEvaluator documents void methods requireView and requireViewClientScopes as Returns true if canView returns true. They return void and throw ForbiddenException on denial. The incorrect contract misleads callers into expecting a boolean result instead of exception-based enforcement.
